question: Does the never-run growth-coupled strain designer in dna_decode/fba/design.py produce a coupled design on its one documented validation target?
headline: 2266 candidate reactions scanned exhaustively as single knockouts against EX_lac__D_e in iML1515. ZERO coupled designs. The code runs correctly -- this is a genuine negative at depth 1, not a plumbing failure.
condition: model default (aerobic if O2 uptake is open)

growth_floor.basis: fraction of EACH strain's OWN maximum growth (standard coupling definition)

why_the_classes_are_not_pooled: POSSIBLE means a growing strain MAY secrete the product (max_product_flux > 0 while min_product_flux is 0). OBLIGATORY means it MUST (min_product_flux > 0). Pooling them would report a wildtype that merely CAN make lactate as a coupled design, which it is not.

wildtype.reading: Wildtype iML1515 CAN secrete D-lactate (max 2.119455) but is not forced to (min 0.0), so it is POSSIBLE and not OBLIGATORY. That is the correct starting point for a coupling search: there is headroom to couple.

best_uncoupled_reading: The best single knockouts the search could find score improvement_over_wildtype 0.0 -- they do not raise the guaranteed product floor at all. Not a near miss: no single reaction knockout moves the minimum product flux off zero.

depth_3_attempt.ended_by: session end, not by the job finishing or erroring
depth_3_attempt.evidence_it_is_not_a_crash: stderr is 0 bytes, so the process emitted no traceback; the output JSON is 0 bytes, so it never reached its single write at the end. It was still running when it was stopped.
depth_3_attempt.why_this_is_itself_informative: Depth 3 enumerates pairs and triples over the most promising singles, but EVERY single in this run scored improvement_over_wildtype 0.0, so the pre-ranking it depends on has no signal to rank by. That is the exact defect pyproject.toml records for this code path.
depth_3_attempt.NOT_claimed: This is NOT evidence that no depth-2 or depth-3 coupled design exists. An unfinished search is an absence of evidence. Only the depth-1 arm is exhaustive.

search_description: all 2266 candidates scanned exhaustively as singles; single reaction knockouts over 2266; only single knockouts searched (max_knockouts=1)
pool_note: all 2266 candidates scanned exhaustively as singles
scope_from_the_code: STOICHIOMETRIC prediction. A coupled design is a HYPOTHESIS FOR THE BENCH, not a validated strain: FBA does not model regulation, enzyme kinetics, toxicity, metabolic burden, or whether the knockout strain is constructible.
depth_1_blindness_caveat_verbatim_from_p: The bounded pair/triple enumeration in `fba/design.py` is exhaustive only at depth 1 and is blind to designs whose members are individually unremarkable -- which is most real ones (see that module's `competition_ranking` for two measured failed attempts to fix it by pre-ranking).

establishes: The designer executes end-to-end on a real genome-scale model and returns a well-formed, internally consistent result. It was never run before today.

At depth 1 the search is EXHAUSTIVE over all 2266 candidates, so the statement that no single-reaction knockout couples D-lactate to growth at a 90 percent growth floor in iML1515 is a measured fact about this model, not a sampling outcome.
251 of the candidates are non-viable at the floor, so the scan is genuinely exercising the growth constraint rather than trivially passing everything.
does_NOT_establish: That no coupled design exists for D-lactate. Depth 1 cannot see multi-knockout designs, and the pyproject caveat above says the enumeration is blind to exactly the designs whose members are individually unremarkable -- which every member here is.
That the MILP arm will also find nothing. It solves the bilevel problem directly instead of enumerating, which is why it is a separate arm of this plan.
Anything about the bench. The scope field quoted above is explicit that a coupled design would be a hypothesis for the bench, not a validated strain.

consequence_for_the_plan: This result PROMOTES the MILP arm (Steps 3-4) from a comparison to the load-bearing test. The enumeration arm has now returned its exhaustive depth-1 answer and its depth-3 arm did not complete, so the open question -- whether iML1515 admits a growth-coupled D-lactate design at all -- now rests entirely on the solver that does not enumerate.
honest_limits: ONE target (D-lactate), ONE model (iML1515), ONE condition (model default, aerobic if the O2 uptake bound is open), ONE growth floor (90 percent). None of these was swept.
Reaction-level knockouts, not gene-level. A reaction knockout is not always realisable by deleting genes, and the gene-to-reaction mapping can make a reaction undeletable.
Depth 3 did not complete, so this artifact reports a depth-1 result only.

The claim that the published growth-coupled lactate strains are DOUBLE knockouts -- which would explain a depth-1 null -- is at SEARCH-SUMMARY level only. Three routes to the primary sources were blocked from this host, so it is labelled as such and is NOT used to interpret this result.
